newsitem.title: UK: Zeneca says sterling impact overestimated.
newsitem.headline: Zeneca says sterling impact overestimated.

text.p: Bioscience company Zeneca Group Plc said on Tuesday that analysts at NatWest Securities had overestimated the impact of the strength of sterling on Zeneca's 1997 earnings.
NatWest analysts were believed to have shaved 140 million stg off their 1997 forecasts for Zeneca to 1.08 billion stg to take account of the pound's strength.
But in an interview with Reuters, Zeneca chief executive David Barnes said the estimate had failed to take into account the impact of currency hedging.
"Because we are approximately 50 percent hedged over the next 12 months, they have overestimated the effect. It is more likely to be 70 to 75 million rather than 140 million," Barnes said.

The downgrade had weighed on Zeneca's share price, which was down 9 pence at 1630 pence in early afternoon trading. NatWest Securities was also reported to have downgraded earnings forecasts for Glaxo Wellcome Plc and SmithKline Beecham Plc on similar grounds.
Zeneca said it is hedged 100 percent on a three-month basis and "at least 50 percent hedged" for the subsequent six months.

Barnes said he was "not concerned" about the pound's current strength. "I don't think the level of sterling is such that our products will be uncompetitive," he said, but added "I do think the pound is getting very fully priced now."
